requirements.requirement: Forward inventory application log messages from node2 to a centralized log collector on node1
requirements.summary: No pre-existing inventory app was found, so the executor created a representative one (systemd service inventory.service on node2 using logger with tag 'inventory', facility local3) and configured rsyslog omfwd forwarding to node1:10514/tcp with a disk-assisted queue. node1 runs an rsyslog imtcp listener on 10514 filtering on source IP and programname. After fixing a firewalld block (No route to host), end-to-end delivery was directly confirmed by tailing accumulating messages on node1 originating from node2's inventory tag.

requirements.requirement: Persist received messages on node1 at /var/log/inventory/node2.log
requirements.summary: Collector rsyslog config on node1 writes filtered inventory messages from node2 to /var/log/inventory/node2.log. Repeated tail/wc commands confirm the file exists, is owned appropriately, and accumulates new lines over time.

requirements.requirement: Log flow keeps working after node1 restarts
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (4326d5b8...) and healthy state captured before reboot; reboot issued; new boot_id (832c5201...) confirmed post-restart, matching the after_executor snapshot. rsyslog, firewalld, and the 10514 listener were confirmed active/recovered automatically (enabled units, no manual restart needed), and after a bounded wait fresh node2-originated log lines with new timestamps were observed appended to /var/log/inventory/node2.log, directly demonstrating restored log flow.

requirements.requirement: Log flow keeps working after node2 restarts
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id (9ed9e820...) and healthy state captured before reboot; reboot issued; new boot_id (346053db...) confirmed post-restart, matching the after_executor snapshot. inventory.service and rsyslog were confirmed active (both enabled, recovered automatically), a fresh verification message was sent from node2, and node1's log file was observed to contain that exact post-reboot message plus continuing stock-sync entries, directly demonstrating restored forwarding.

overall_summary: The executor built a representative inventory application on node2 (since none pre-existed), configured rsyslog-based centralized forwarding to node1 over TCP/10514, persisted matching messages to /var/log/inventory/node2.log, diagnosed and fixed a firewalld block, and directly demonstrated end-to-end delivery. Both node1 and node2 were independently rebooted with boot-id verification, automatic recovery of all relevant services, and confirmed resumption of log delivery afterward, satisfying the restart-durability requirement with direct before/during/after evidence. All four material outcomes are satisfied.
limitations: The inventory application itself was fabricated by the executor since no pre-existing app was found on either node; this is a reasonable interpretation of an ambiguous task but means the forwarding logic is tied to a synthetic app rather than a real one.

Some log timestamps in the tailed output (e.g., 'Aug 26 10:36...') appear to be stale/pre-existing image clock artifacts mixed with correct Sep 29 entries; this did not affect the ability to confirm delivery but is a minor data-quality oddity worth noting.
Small residual /tmp/reboot.log files were left on both nodes after the reboot commands; low-risk but not cleaned up.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to the task: creating the placeholder inventory app/service on node2 (cmd-d4df999b18d7457d), the rsyslog collector config and directory on node1 (cmd-36201a015f574b23), the forwarding config on node2 (cmd-28c5eb7519ee4938), the necessary firewalld port opening on node1 to fix a diagnosed connectivity failure (cmd-50283631ef534c29), and the two bounded reboots used both to satisfy the restart-survivability requirement and the provider-wide restart protocol (cmd-39dc065b2b6542fb, cmd-2f640d9631974824). Earlier failed attempts without sudo (cmd-5de60b1cbae54c1d, cmd-afd104f7b36b46f7) made no state changes (permission denied). One minor artifact of note: the reboot invocation left /tmp/reboot.log on both node1 and node2 after restart (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot); this is a small, low-risk, unreverted residue rather than an unnecessary broad mutation.
